chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal from al-Abbas ibn Aamir from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a slave girl, lies with her seeking offspring, but is not granted a child from her. So he gifts her to his brother or sells her, and she bears him children. Can his son from another woman marry the daughter of his brother from her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' So I repeated it to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.أَزْوَاجُ: Marriages (implied in the question of marrying)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible
key_terms.يَقَعُ عَلَيْهَا: He lies with her (consummates the relationship)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his half-sister from the same mother but different father?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of marriage between half-siblings sharing a mother but having different fathers, specifically addressing the scenario of a slave girl transferred between brothers. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that the maternal bond alone does not create an impediment (لا بأس به) for the sons to marry each other's daughters, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the prohibition of marriage applies to full and half-siblings through the father or mother, but cross-lineage unions are permissible. This ruling underscores the flexibility in marital laws regarding enslaved women in early Islamic society, where ownership and lineage could be distinct.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwa, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Asimy, form Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Fazzal, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Shuayb Al Aqarquqy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have the slave girl for him. He fell upon her seeking her child, but was not Graced with a child from her. So he gifted her to his brother, or sold her, so she gave birth to children for him. Can his children from other than her marry the children of his brother from her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> told me to repeat it, so I repeated it to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said : ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Asemiy from Ali ibn al-Hassan Faddal from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu’ayb al-‘Aqarqufiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has a slave-girl with whom he goes to bed seeking to have a child, but does not become fortunate to have a child and gives her to his brother as a gift or sells her and she gives birth to several children; if his children from a woman other than her can marry the children of his brother from her. He (the Imam) asked me to say it again. I said it again and he (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is not unlawful.’”
